verification.summary: Both must-fix items from the last round are fixed — the ACCS now groups the log into repaint blocks and checks the final block holds every issue exactly once with correct counts, which a diff-style repainter can't fake.

shouldFix.problem: Only the final repaint block is checked for full-list shape; an implementation that diffs on earlier cycles and only does a full repaint on the last one would still pass. Fine for this spec's purposes, just not airtight across the whole run.

shouldKnow.problem: Block separation relies on non-matching lines (e.g. clear-screen codes or log lines) interrupting the Issue-line runs; if a real implementation ever prints issue lines back-to-back across two repaints with nothing in between, they'd merge into one block and undercount cycles. Low risk given the assumed clear+reprint behavior, just worth knowing.

application.summary: Added the mutation endpoint (GET/POST /issues, /issues/:number/comments) and a repainting GitHub Service Terminal to the mock GitHub service, plus a new Proactive Issues Tracker that mock-mode-gates itself and drops a one-time 'I've been here!' comment per undiscovered issue. specs/002-early-alpha-issues-reader/output/accs.bash passes on repeated runs, and pnpm typecheck/lint/format:check/test all pass.

picks.decision: cadence of the GitHub Service Terminal's repaint loop
picks.why: the contract only says every poll tick and every accepted comment trigger a repaint, and the mock service has no 'poll' of its own — a steady 1s tick is the simplest thing that gives the ACCS multiple repaint blocks inside its 4s window

picks.decision: how to make repaint cycles distinguishable in the log
picks.chose: print a timestamped header line before each block of Issue #n lines
picks.why: without a non-matching separator, back-to-back full repaints of the same issue list are indistinguishable from one continuous list when read back later

picks.decision: what happens to an issue whose marker-comment POST fails
picks.chose: un-touch it so the next poll retries, rather than giving up permanently
picks.why: no persistence exists anywhere in this spec, so silently abandoning an issue forever on one transient failure seemed worse than a bounded retry loop

findings.problem: Applying this as the code default would change what port `pnpm mock-github` binds to when MOCK_GITHUB_PORT is unset, which breaks spec 001's accs.bash (it never sets MOCK_GITHUB_PORT itself and hardcodes port 4123) — and spec 002's own ACCS runs spec 001's ACCS first as a gate. I left the code default at 4123 so both ACCS suites keep passing; spec 002's own runs are unaffected since its accs.bash always sets MOCK_GITHUB_PORT explicitly.
